quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Two actions overlap here — one was already happening ('was waiting') when the second one interrupted it.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + was waiting (past continuous) + at the airport (place) + when her flight was cancelled (interrupting clause). Use past continuous for an action already in progress, and simple past for the shorter action that interrupts it.
quests.textToSpeak: She was waiting at the airport when her flight was cancelled.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Was cooking' sets the ongoing scene; the shorter action comes right after 'when'.
quests.explanation: Subject (He) + was cooking (past continuous) + dinner (object) + when his daughter called from college (interrupting clause). The longer background action uses past continuous; the sudden event uses simple past.
quests.textToSpeak: He was cooking dinner when his daughter called from college.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'The teacher'. The interrupting event follows 'when'.
quests.explanation: Subject (The teacher) + was grading (past continuous) + papers (object) + when the fire alarm rang (interrupting clause). 'Rang' is the irregular past tense of 'ring'.
quests.textToSpeak: The teacher was grading papers when the fire alarm rang.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'So' connects a problem to the result it caused.
quests.explanation: Cause (He felt dizzy) + so (result connector) + effect (he decided to see a doctor). 'So' links a cause to its natural result.
quests.textToSpeak: He felt dizzy, so he decided to see a doctor.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'But' introduces a contrast to what you might expect.
quests.explanation: Setup (She was tired) + but (contrast connector) + unexpected result (she still finished cleaning the kitchen). 'But' shows the second idea goes against the first.
quests.textToSpeak: She was tired, but she still finished cleaning the kitchen.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Because' introduces the reason at the end of the sentence.
quests.explanation: Result (He worked late) + because (reason connector) + cause (the deadline was the next morning). 'Because' clauses explain why something happened.
quests.textToSpeak: He worked late because the deadline was the next morning.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Although' opens the sentence with an unexpected fact; a comma marks where the main idea begins.
quests.explanation: Concession (Although the flight was delayed) + main clause (they still made their connection). 'Although' at the start of a sentence is followed by a comma before the main clause.
quests.textToSpeak: Although the flight was delayed, they still made their connection.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: This time 'although' sits in the middle, with no comma needed before it.
quests.explanation: Main clause (She enjoyed the concert) + although (contrast connector) + concession (the seats were quite far). 'Although' can open a sentence or sit in the middle.
quests.textToSpeak: She enjoyed the concert, although the seats were quite far.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Kept crashing' means the crashing happened again and again.
quests.explanation: Result (He updated the app) + because (reason connector) + cause (it kept crashing suddenly). 'Keep + verb-ing' describes a repeated action.
quests.textToSpeak: He updated the app because it kept crashing suddenly.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Told me that' introduces someone else's words indirectly.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + told me that (reporting verb) + her brother was moving to Canada (reported clause). In reported speech, 'that' can introduce the shared information.
quests.textToSpeak: She told me that her brother was moving to Canada.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: The reported event happened before the mentioning, so it uses 'had been'.
quests.explanation: Subject (He) + mentioned that (reporting verb) + the meeting had been moved to Friday (reported clause). 'Had been moved' shows the change happened before he mentioned it.
quests.textToSpeak: He mentioned that the meeting had been moved to Friday.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'No longer' means something that used to be true isn't anymore.
quests.explanation: Subject (The waiter) + explained that (reporting verb) + the soup was no longer available (reported clause). 'No longer' signals a change from an earlier state.
quests.textToSpeak: The waiter explained that the soup was no longer available.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'While' introduces the background action in progress.
quests.explanation: Background action (While volunteers were painting the fence) + main event (neighbors brought them lemonade). 'While' pairs naturally with past continuous to set a scene.
quests.textToSpeak: While volunteers were painting the fence, neighbors brought them lemonade.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: The ongoing activity comes first; the sudden injury interrupts it.
quests.explanation: Background action (While she was jogging in the park) + interrupting event (she twisted her ankle). The comma separates the introductory clause from the main clause.
quests.textToSpeak: While she was jogging in the park, she twisted her ankle.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: Start with 'While'. The unexpected event follows the comma.
quests.explanation: Background action (While the students were taking the exam) + interrupting event (the power went out). 'Go out' here means to stop working, used for lights or electricity.
quests.textToSpeak: While the students were taking the exam, the power went out.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Managed to' shows success despite a difficulty.
quests.explanation: Subject (They) + managed to find (verb phrase) + a taxi (object) + even though it was raining (contrast clause). 'Manage to + verb' means to succeed at something difficult.
quests.textToSpeak: They managed to find a taxi even though it was raining.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Without + verb-ing' shows what she avoided doing.
quests.explanation: Subject (She) + managed to fix (verb phrase) + the printer (object) + without calling for help (manner). 'Without + verb-ing' describes an action done in the absence of something else.
quests.textToSpeak: She managed to fix the printer without calling for help.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Used to' describes a repeated past habit that has since stopped.
quests.explanation: Subject (He) + used to visit (past habit) + his grandparents (object) + every single summer (frequency). 'Used to + verb' describes something that regularly happened in the past but doesn't now.
quests.textToSpeak: He used to visit his grandparents every single summer.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Used to' contrasts with 'now' to show a change over time.
quests.explanation: Past habit (She used to hate vegetables) + but (contrast) + present state (now she loves them). This pattern is ideal for describing how feelings change over time.
quests.textToSpeak: She used to hate vegetables, but now she loves them.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: The background activity comes first; the interruption follows 'when'.
quests.explanation: Subject (He) + was watching (past continuous) + the game (object) + when his phone started ringing (interrupting clause). 'Start + verb-ing' emphasizes the beginning of an action.
quests.textToSpeak: He was watching the game when his phone started ringing.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Because' explains the technical cause.
quests.explanation: Result (The website crashed) + because (reason connector) + cause (too many people logged in). 'Log in' is a common phrasal verb for accessing an online account.
quests.textToSpeak: The website crashed because too many people logged in.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Said that' introduces reported information calmly and directly.
quests.explanation: Subject (The doctor) + said that (reporting verb) + the results looked completely normal (reported clause). 'Looked' here means 'appeared to be', based on what the results showed.
quests.textToSpeak: The doctor said that the results looked completely normal.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: The reported fact describes a regular schedule, so it stays in simple past.
quests.explanation: Subject (The guide) + explained that (reporting verb) + the museum closed early on Sundays (reported clause). Regular schedules and general facts often stay in simple past in reported speech.
quests.textToSpeak: The guide explained that the museum closed early on Sundays.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Would' is the reported form of 'will' when talking about the future.
quests.explanation: Subject (The manager) + announced that (reporting verb) + the office would close for renovations (reported clause). 'Will' in direct speech becomes 'would' in reported speech.
quests.textToSpeak: The manager announced that the office would close for renovations.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Even though' is a stronger version of 'although'.
quests.explanation: Concession (Even though it was late) + main clause (she called her mother anyway). 'Even though' emphasizes the contrast more strongly than 'although' alone.
quests.textToSpeak: Even though it was late, she called her mother anyway.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Still' reinforces that the event happened despite the obstacle.
quests.explanation: Concession (Even though the rain continued) + main clause (the parade still went ahead). 'Still' adds emphasis to show something happened despite a difficulty.
quests.textToSpeak: Even though the rain continued, the parade still went ahead.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: The comma marks the boundary between the concession and the result.
quests.explanation: Concession (Even though tickets were expensive) + main clause (the show sold out quickly). 'Sold out' means every ticket was purchased.
quests.textToSpeak: Even though tickets were expensive, the show sold out quickly.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Kept dropping' means the signal failed again and again.
quests.explanation: Result (She switched phone plans) + because (reason connector) + cause (the signal kept dropping). 'Keep + verb-ing' shows a repeated, frustrating pattern.
quests.textToSpeak: She switched phone plans because the signal kept dropping.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: 'Much closer' is a comparative describing distance.
quests.explanation: Result (He joined a new gym) + because (reason connector) + cause (it was much closer). 'Much' intensifies the comparative adjective 'closer'.
quests.textToSpeak: He joined a new gym because it was much closer.

quests.instruction: Listen to the audio and arrange the words in the correct order.
quests.hint: The reason clause explains the motivation behind the move.
quests.explanation: Result (They moved to a smaller house) + because (reason connector) + cause (the rent increased). 'Increase' as a verb means to become larger in amount.
quests.textToSpeak: They moved to a smaller house because the rent increased.
